rationale: The largest blind spot the ontology measurement found in this lane, and it is a grammar fact rather than a walk bug: 125 `@extend` tokens across 4,394 admitted corpus files and only 36 `extend_statement` nodes, so 71% of them are in the recovered shape `block > ERROR > "@extend", placeholder, ";"`. A `.card { @extend %badge; }` — which is where a BEM codebase puts nearly every `@extend` — produced NO edge at all, because the statement's own node type never appears and the keyword survives only as an anonymous token the named-children walk skips. 63 of the 99 real `@extend`s were invisible before this. Three separate things are pinned here because they fail independently. (1) The recovered `@extend` INSIDE A RULE BODY emits an edge from the rule to the placeholder it names, marked `scssRecoveredFromError`, because a claim read out of a broken region is real and a consumer deserves to know it was recovered. (2) `%placeholder` is an endpoint that RESOLVES — it is a selector the CSS lane already publishes, so `@extend %badge` and the `%badge` rule join. (3) The INTERPOLATED form `@extend %responsive-#{$bp}` emits NOTHING: the grammar cuts the placeholder at the interpolation, so its text is the prefix `%responsive-`, which names no selector and resolves to no symbol. A forbidden row pins that, because an edge to a prefix is the phantom-endpoint defect this lane has removed twice and it would look like progress. `%row`/`%col` are extended from two different rules so the two rules cannot be collapsed into one row that passes when only the first works.
